subject: Portal evidence ingest accelerator and short checklist
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@heliosecurity.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Portal evidence ingest accelerator and short checklist

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for agreeing to help accelerate our profile setup in Vendr. To keep the initial onboarding tight and minimize back-and-forth, I put together a short two-step plan and attached a small manifest and the ingest playbook we discussed: redwood-ingest-manifest-v1.csv and ingest-playbook-v1.pdf.

High level (proposed):
- Step 1 (incremental): Push a light subset of CAIQ + SIG artifacts (controls mapping, SOC2 summary, encryption proof) so we can validate the mapping and surface any field mapping gaps.
- Step 2 (bulk): After Step 1 is validated, do a bulk ingest of the remaining artifacts and the signed evidence bundle.

Questions for your team — can you confirm which of these two ingestion paths you prefer and the recommended credentialing method (Vendr API token vs. temporary SFTP bucket)? If Vendr API is preferred, can you create a short-lived token and share the transfer location/headers? We prefer an API for automation, but SFTP works if that’s simpler for initial uploads.

Proposed windows (PT):
- Thu May 13, 10:00–11:00 PT (validation run)
- Mon May 17, 14:00–16:00 PT (bulk ingest)

Please see the attached manifest for file naming expectations and a sample row. If the manifest doesn't align with your ingestion schema, point us to the example layout and we’ll reformat.

Also cc’ing Ben for scheduling and Naomi for CAIQ/SIG mapping questions.

Thanks — looking forward to a quick run.

—
Michael Grant
Sr. Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood-ingest-manifest-v1.csv (csv), ingest-playbook-v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@heliosecurity.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, procurement@heliosecurity.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Portal evidence ingest accelerator and short checklist

Hi Michael —

Appreciate the clear plan and the manifest — this is straightforward and aligns with how we normally stage Vendr imports. Two quick notes:

1) Credentialing: We can do Vendr API token or temporary SFTP. For repeatable automation we recommend an API token (we’ll issue a token scoped to uploads only). If you prefer SFTP, we’ll provide host + creds and a pre-populated upload dir.

2) Minimal schema differences: Your manifest schema is fine. The only field we commonly see missing is the ‘control_evidence_type’ enum (pdf, gist, screenshot). If you can provide that column we can avoid a manual QC pass.

I attached a tiny API credential template and a sample upload map — see api-credentials-template.txt.

We can run the validation window on Thu May 13 at 10:00 PT. I’ll create a temp upload token and post the details to this thread by EOD today.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Integration Lead, Helio Security
olivia@heliosecurity.com

Attachments: api-credentials-template.txt (txt)

Thanks — small ask from my side: can we prioritize the CAIQ control_id alignment in the validation run? If Helio can flag any controls that map to multiple fields on Vendr (we’ve had ambiguous mappings for encryption key lifecycle before), we should capture those in the validation sprint so the bulk ingest doesn’t stall.

I’ve dropped a quick pointer to our CAIQ mapping doc here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cCAIQ-mapping — Naomi, can you skim the manifest and add the control_evidence_type column if convenient?

—Ben
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
